search_scope: Bounded search for author/provider-published historical biotech company acquisition targets and comparison outcomes with financial features and an explicit sample definition. This is not an exhaustive census.
conclusion: No inspected source establishes a usable biotech historical prediction panel under the repository validation contract. A real provider-published broad-market target/peer financial sample was downloaded and pinned for methodology inspection; its peer labels are not accepted 12-month negative outcomes.

downloaded_all_data_inspection.biotech_count_note: The notebook drops TRBC industry before saving; absence of a biotech string is not evidence of zero biotech companies.

sample_definition.peer_assignment: Peers of retained targets receive Label=0; concatenation places targets first, then removes duplicate RIC prefixes. No per-company 12-month outcome search is implemented.
sample_definition.financial_request_date: Target announcement minus 30 calendar days; peers share target-relative dates.
sample_definition.observation_selection: Dates selected retrospectively relative to known target events; no prospectively specified common company cohorts.
sample_definition.validation_in_notebook: Repeated stratified cross-validation; no chronological purged holdout.

limitations: Peer label0 lacks full prospective 12-month ascertainment and could hide unselected or later deals.
Broad-market sample, sector field removed, no historical biotech-membership evidence.
Provider SDate query alone does not archive filing publication times or original-as-filed versus restatement lineage.
Reported nonfinancial AR feature uses returns closer to the event than AD-30, so AD-30 cannot be declared the availability time for all features.
Notebook hard-coded narrative total3849 disagrees with actual3830 rows and its own182+3648 counts.
No explicit standalone data license was found in the inspected repository root; public download is not proof of unrestricted redistribution rights.
sources.allowed_use_in_this_delivery: Pinned source catalogue and methodological research only; no labels or features imported into training.
